replies_you_may_hear: I want a refund for the delivery. · This is the second time. · I needed it for an event.
if_customer_pushes: Customer: "Sorry is not enough." → Agent: "You're right, an apology alone is not enough. I have refunded your delivery charge, and I've reported the delay to our courier partner."
cultural_note: "I am writing to complain" is standard formal English, not an Indian-English phrase. International customers who use it usually expect a personal reply, so treat it as a formal complaint, not a casual question.
channel_note: Voice: "I'm calling to make a complaint." Chat: "I want to complain." Email: the formal line often means the customer may escalate if the reply is weak.
when_not_to_use: Do not send a canned "thank you for your feedback" reply to a message that starts with "I am writing to complain".
mini_conversation: Customer: I am writing to complain about my late delivery. | Agent: I'm sorry your order arrived a week late, Ms Clarke. | Customer: I needed it for my son's birthday. | Agent: I understand how disappointing that was. I have refunded the delivery charge.
source_rule: Apologise specifically and take responsibility, then offer a fix.
fill_blank: I am very unhappy, so I am writing to ____ about my late delivery.
mcq_question: A customer's email begins "I am writing to complain about my late delivery." What does this line show?

mcq_why: "Complain" in a formal opening shows real dissatisfaction. B and C do not match what the line says, and D is tempting because companies call it "feedback", but the customer wants action, not thanks.
reorder_task: complain / to / writing / am / I
reorder_answer: I am writing to complain.

role_play: Partner A writes a short formal complaint about a late delivery. Partner B reads it, says in one line what A feels and wants, then writes the first three lines of a reply.

sentence: Please find attached the invoice.
speaker: Customer
situation: A customer is asking for a refund on a damaged coffee maker and has added their purchase invoice to the email.
recall_cue: The customer says a document is with their email. What should you do before you write back?
linking: If read aloud: find_attached → "fain-da-tacht" · attached_the → "a-tach-the"
intonation: If read aloud: flat and falling; it is a formal note, not a request for action.
indian_pron_tip: If you read it aloud, "attached" is a-TACHT (two syllables), not "a-tach-ed"; "invoice" has a clear "v" (top teeth on the lower lip).
customer_emotion: Organised and expecting the document to be used.
memory_hook: "Find attached" means "look at the paperclip": open the file before you reply.
hindi_meaning: कृपया संलग्न इनवॉइस देखें।
hindi_roman: Kripya sanlagn invoice dekhein.
simple_meaning: I have added the bill to this email; please look at it.
why_it_works: The customer has already sent what you will need. They expect you to open it and use it, not to ask for it again.
key_chunk: Please find attached ___.
grammar_pattern: Please + find + attached + noun
grammar_note: "Attached" works like an adjective here: "find the invoice (that is) attached".
tone_note: It is formal but normal business English. Reply in a friendly, plain way, and never ask for a document the customer already sent.
watch_out: ✗ Please share the invoice. (it is already attached) → ✓ Thank you for sending the invoice. I can see you bought the coffee maker on 3 May.
dont_say: "Please send your invoice to proceed." — asking again for a file the customer attached shows you did not read the email.
positive_swap: Instead of "Please send the invoice", write "Thank you for the invoice. I can see your purchase on 3 May."
alt_1: I have attached the invoice.
alt_2: The invoice is attached.
more_formal: Please find the invoice attached for your reference.
ask_next: Thank you for sending the invoice. I can see you bought the coffee maker on 3 May, and I'm checking your refund now.
replies_you_may_hear: Can you confirm you got it? · Is that enough proof? · I've also added photos.
if_customer_pushes: Customer: "I already sent the invoice, why are you asking again?" → Agent: "You're right, and I'm sorry I asked for it again. I've found it now, and I'll confirm your refund by 5 pm today."
cultural_note: "Please find attached" is a normal formal phrase in both Indian and international business English. The problem is only "the same" in place of the document name.
channel_note: Voice: the customer may say "I've emailed you the invoice." Chat: "I've uploaded the invoice." Email: always open the attachment before replying.
when_not_to_use: Do not reply "Noted" without checking that the attachment opens and is the right document.
mini_conversation: Customer: My coffee maker broke. Please find attached the invoice. | Agent: Thank you for the invoice. I can see your purchase on 3 May, and I'm sorry the coffee maker broke. | Customer: Great, can I get a refund? | Agent: I'm checking it now, and I'll email you by 5 pm today.
source_rule: Use plain words and give one clear next step.
fill_blank: Please find ____ (starts with a) the invoice.
mcq_question: The customer writes "Please find attached the invoice." What should you do first?
mcq_options: A) Open the attachment and check the purchase details before you reply. | B) Reply asking them to send the invoice again so that you can check it. | C) Close the ticket, because the customer has sent everything you need. | D) Reply asking for a photo of the invoice so that you can see the date.
mcq_why: The invoice is already in the email. B and D are tempting if you skim the email, but asking again shows you did not read it, and C closes the case before anyone has looked at the invoice.
reorder_task: attached / find / invoice / Please / the
reorder_answer: Please find attached the invoice.
hindi_to_english: Customer ko thanks kahiye invoice bhejne ke liye aur bataiye ki aapko 3 May ki purchase dikh rahi hai.
hindi_to_english_answer: Thank you for sending the invoice. I can see your purchase on 3 May.
whats_next_customer: Did you get the invoice? I'm not sure it was attached.
whats_next_reply: Yes, I received it, thank you. It shows your purchase on 3 May.
role_play: Partner A sends an email with "Please find attached the invoice" and a photo of a bill. Partner B replies confirming the document, one detail from it, and the next step.
record_task: Write a reply to a customer who attached their invoice: confirm you received it, mention one detail from it and give the next step. Send it as text or a photo for audit.
self_check: Did you confirm you received the attachment? · Did you mention a detail from it? · Did you avoid asking for it again?

sentence: Kindly do the needful.
speaker: Customer
situation: A customer explains that their address is wrong on an order and ends the email with this line.
recall_cue: An email ends with a common Indian-English request. What is the customer actually asking you to do?
linking: If read aloud: do_the → "doo-the" · the_needful → "the-need-ful"
intonation: If read aloud: flat and falling; it is a polite closing request.
indian_pron_tip: If you read the line aloud, say "the" with a soft "th" (tongue between the teeth), not "de".
customer_emotion: Polite and expecting quick action.
memory_hook: "The needful" is a blank box: the customer has already written what goes in it earlier in the email.
hindi_meaning: कृपया जो ज़रूरी है वह कर दीजिए।
hindi_roman: Kripya jo zaroori hai woh kar dijiye.
simple_meaning: Please take whatever action is needed to fix my problem.
why_it_works: The customer is being polite and expects you to do the obvious next step, which is usually in the lines before. Reply by naming the exact action you took.
key_chunk: do the needful
grammar_pattern: Kindly + do + the + needful
grammar_note: "The needful" means "what is necessary"; it is a set phrase in Indian English.
tone_note: It is polite and normal in Indian English. Do not copy it back; just say clearly what you have done.
watch_out: ✗ I have change your delivery address. → ✓ I have changed your delivery address to 14 Lake Road.
dont_say: "Noted, the needful will be done." — it does not say what you will do, so the customer still does not know if the address is fixed.
positive_swap: Instead of "We will do the needful", write "I have changed your delivery address to 14 Lake Road."
alt_1: Please take the necessary action.
alt_2: Please look into this and fix it.
more_formal: I would be grateful if you could take the necessary action.
ask_next: I have changed your delivery address to 14 Lake Road, and your order is now due to arrive on Thursday.
replies_you_may_hear: Thank you for the quick help. · Please confirm once done. · When will it be delivered now?
if_customer_pushes: Customer: "Please confirm the needful is done." → Agent: "Yes, it's done. Your order now shows 14 Lake Road as the address, and it is due to arrive on Thursday."
cultural_note: Many Indian customers use "do the needful" politely; it is a long-standing Indian English phrase. International readers may find it old-fashioned, so agents should switch to naming the action.
channel_note: Voice: "Please do the needful" means "please sort it out". Chat: same. Email: reply with the exact action and a confirmation.
when_not_to_use: Do not guess the action if the email does not say what is wrong; ask one clear question instead.
mini_conversation: Customer: My address is wrong on order 39054. Kindly do the needful. | Agent: I have changed your delivery address to 14 Lake Road. | Customer: Thank you. When will it come? | Agent: It is due to arrive on Thursday.
source_rule: Indian English switch: for "do the needful", say the actual action.
fill_blank: Kindly do the ____ (ends in -ful).
mcq_question: A customer writes about a wrong address and ends with "Kindly do the needful." What do they want?
mcq_options: A) A form to fill in so that the address can be changed later. | B) A refund, because the order was sent to the wrong address. | C) A call from a manager to discuss the problem with the order. | D) For you to correct the address on their order and confirm it.
mcq_why: "The needful" points back to the problem in the email, which is the wrong address, so the action is to fix it and confirm. B is tempting because a wrong address can end in a refund, but the customer has not asked for one, and A and C add steps nobody requested.
reorder_task: address / changed / your / I / delivery / have
reorder_answer: I have changed your delivery address.
hindi_to_english: Customer ko bataiye ki aapne unka phone number update kar diya hai.
hindi_to_english_answer: I have updated your phone number on the account.
whats_next_customer: Thanks. Will I get a tracking link for the new address?
whats_next_reply: Yes, I will email you the tracking link today. The courier now shows delivery on Thursday.
role_play: Partner A writes a short email about a wrong billing name ending in "Kindly do the needful." Partner B replies by naming the exact action taken, without copying the phrase.
record_task: Write a reply to a customer whose email ends "Kindly do the needful" after asking to change their delivery date; name the exact action you took. Send it as text or a photo for audit.
self_check: Did you find the real request in the email? · Did you name the exact action? · Did you avoid copying "do the needful" back, as international customers may not expect it?

sentence: Further to my previous email, I still have not received my refund.
speaker: Customer
situation: A customer wrote last week about a refund and is now writing again because the money has not arrived.
recall_cue: The customer points back to an earlier email. What should you check before you reply?
linking: If read aloud: further_to → "fur-ther-tuh" · still_have → "sti-lhav"
intonation: If read aloud: firm and falling, with stress on "still" and "not".
indian_pron_tip: If you read it aloud, "further" has a soft "th" in the middle (tongue between the teeth), not "fur-der".
customer_emotion: Impatient and losing trust because nothing has happened.
memory_hook: "Further to" is a finger pointing back: scroll down and read the first email before you type a word.
hindi_meaning: मेरे पिछले ईमेल के संदर्भ में, मुझे अभी तक मेरा रिफ़ंड नहीं मिला है।
hindi_roman: Mere pichhle email ke sandarbh mein, mujhe abhi tak mera refund nahin mila hai.
simple_meaning: I wrote to you before, and I am writing again because my money has still not come back.
why_it_works: The customer is pointing back to their earlier email. They want you to know the history without explaining again, plus a clear answer with a date.
key_chunk: Further to my previous email, ___.
grammar_pattern: Further to + my + previous + noun + , + statement
grammar_note: "Further to" is a formal way to say "about what I wrote before".
tone_note: "Still" shows impatience. Reply with an apology for the wait and a real date; a fresh template that asks them to explain again will make them angrier.
watch_out: ✗ Please share your issue in detail. → ✓ I'm sorry your refund hasn't arrived yet. I've checked your first email and the refund status.
dont_say: "Please raise a new request." — it ignores the history and makes the customer start again.
positive_swap: Instead of "Please explain your issue", write "I'm sorry you're still waiting. I've read your first email and checked your refund."
alt_1: I'm writing again about my refund, which I still haven't received.
alt_2: Following up on my last email: the refund has not reached me yet.
more_formal: With reference to my earlier email, I wish to inform you that I have not yet received my refund.
ask_next: I'm sorry you're still waiting. Your refund was sent on 2 June, and it should reach your card by 9 June.
replies_you_may_hear: That's what you said last time. · Can you send proof it was sent? · Why does it take so long?
if_customer_pushes: Customer: "That's what you said last time." → Agent: "I understand why you're frustrated. Here is the refund reference number, RF-57340, which your bank can use to trace the payment. I'll check again on 9 June and email you."
cultural_note: "Further to" is used in both Indian and international formal email. It always means the customer has written before, so read the whole thread first.
channel_note: Voice: "I called last week about my refund." Chat: "I already asked about this yesterday." Email: the earlier message is usually below, so scroll down.
when_not_to_use: Do not reply with the same answer as last time without new information; give a date, a reference number or an action.
mini_conversation: Customer: Further to my previous email, I still have not received my refund. | Agent: I'm sorry you're still waiting. It was sent on 2 June and should reach your card by 9 June. | Customer: Can you prove it was sent? | Agent: Yes, the refund reference number is RF-57340.
source_rule: Follow-ups: treat it as the same issue, not a new one; give a real time.
fill_blank: ____ to my previous email, I still have not received my refund.
mcq_question: Your system shows this as a new ticket with no history, but the email begins "Further to my previous email, …". What should you do first?
mcq_options: A) Treat it as a new request and ask the customer to explain the problem from the start. | B) Reply with the usual refund steps from the help centre and close the ticket. | C) Wait until the customer writes a third time before you look into the refund. | D) Find the customer's earlier email, read it and check the refund before you reply.
mcq_why: "Further to" points back to an earlier email, so find it and check the refund before you answer. A is tempting because the ticket looks new in your system, but it makes the customer start again; B ignores the history and C leaves them waiting longer.
reorder_task: received / have / my / not / I / refund / still
reorder_answer: I still have not received my refund.
hindi_to_english: Customer se maafi maangiye ki woh abhi bhi refund ka intezaar kar rahe hain, aur date bataiye.
hindi_to_english_answer: I'm sorry you're still waiting. Your refund should reach your card by 9 June.
whats_next_customer: Can you send proof that it was sent?
whats_next_reply: Yes. The refund reference number is RF-57340; your bank can use it to trace the payment.
role_play: Partner A sends a second email starting "Further to my previous email" about a missing replacement. Partner B reads the history and replies with an apology, the status and a date.
record_task: Write a reply to a customer who writes "Further to my previous email, I still have not received my replacement." Include an apology, the status and a date. Send it as text or a photo for audit.
self_check: Did you read the earlier email first? · Did you apologise for the wait? · Did you give a real date or reference?

sentence: I look forward to your reply.
speaker: Customer
situation: A customer ends an email asking whether a sofa can be delivered on a Sunday.
recall_cue: An email ends with a polite formal closing. What does the customer expect from you, and how soon?
linking: If read aloud: look_forward → "loo-kfor-ward" · forward_to → "for-wer-duh"
intonation: If read aloud: polite and falling; it is a closing line, not a question.
indian_pron_tip: If you read it aloud, "forward" is FOR-wud with a soft "w" (rounded lips, no teeth), not "for-vard".
customer_emotion: Calm and expecting a clear answer soon.
memory_hook: "Look forward" means the customer is looking at the door, waiting for your reply to walk in.
hindi_meaning: मैं आपके जवाब का इंतज़ार कर रहा/रही हूँ।
hindi_roman: Main aapke jawaab ka intezaar kar raha/rahi hoon.
simple_meaning: I am waiting for you to answer this email.
why_it_works: It is a polite formal ending, not a complaint. The customer simply expects a clear answer to their question within a normal time.
key_chunk: I look forward to ___.
grammar_pattern: I look forward + to + noun / verb-ing
grammar_note: After "look forward to", use a noun or an -ing verb: "to your reply" or "to hearing from you".
tone_note: It is polite and neutral, not pushy. Reply to the actual question; there is no need to copy this line back.
watch_out: ✗ I look forward to hear from you. → ✓ I look forward to hearing from you.
dont_say: "Noted." as the whole reply — it does not answer the question the customer is waiting on.
positive_swap: Instead of "Noted, will check", write "I've checked, and we can deliver your sofa this Sunday between 9 am and 1 pm."
alt_1: Hope to hear from you soon.
alt_2: Waiting for your answer.
more_formal: I look forward to hearing from you at your earliest convenience.
ask_next: Thanks for your question. I've checked, and we can deliver your sofa this Sunday between 9 am and 1 pm.
replies_you_may_hear: Thanks for the quick reply. · Great, please book it. · Can you do the morning?
if_customer_pushes: Customer: "I'm still waiting for a reply." → Agent: "I'm sorry you had to wait for a reply. I've checked, and Sunday delivery is possible; shall I book this Sunday between 9 am and 1 pm?"
cultural_note: "I look forward to your reply" is standard formal English everywhere, so there is no switch to make when you read it. The slip to avoid in your own writing is "look forward to hear"; the standard form is "look forward to hearing".
channel_note: Voice: "I'll wait for your call." Chat: rare. Email: a normal formal ending; answer the question in the first line of your reply.
when_not_to_use: Do not read this line as urgent or angry; it is a standard polite ending.
mini_conversation: Customer: Can you deliver the sofa on Sunday? I look forward to your reply. | Agent: Yes, I've checked, and we can deliver it this Sunday between 9 am and 1 pm. | Customer: Great, please book it. | Agent: Done. You'll get a confirmation text on Saturday.
source_rule: Email body: answer clearly and give one clear next step.
fill_blank: I look forward ____ your reply.
mcq_question: A customer ends with "I look forward to your reply." What does this show?
mcq_options: A) The customer is angry and wants a manager to reply to the email. | B) The customer wants a phone call instead of an email reply. | C) The customer is cancelling the order and wants it confirmed. | D) It is a polite formal ending; the customer expects a clear answer.
mcq_why: It is a standard polite ending that expects an answer. A is tempting because the line is formal, but there is no anger in it, and B and C say something the line never says.
reorder_task: forward / I / reply / to / look / your
reorder_answer: I look forward to your reply.
hindi_to_english: Customer ke sawaal ka jawaab dijiye: sawaal ke liye dhanyavaad, haan, hum Saturday ko delivery kar sakte hain.
hindi_to_english_answer: Thanks for your question. Yes, we can deliver on Saturday.
whats_next_customer: Great, please book it for the morning.
whats_next_reply: Done. I have booked your sofa for this Sunday between 9 am and 1 pm, and you will get a confirmation email today.
role_play: Partner A emails asking if a fridge can be installed on the same day as delivery, ending "I look forward to your reply." Partner B answers the question in the first line and gives the next step.
record_task: Write a reply to a customer who asks about Sunday delivery and ends "I look forward to your reply." Answer in the first line. Send it as text or a photo for audit.
self_check: Did you answer the question in the first line? · Did you give a day and time? · Did you avoid a one-word "Noted" reply?

sentence: This is my second email about this.
speaker: Customer
situation: A customer emailed four days ago about a faulty phone charger that you can see is still under warranty, got no reply, and has written again.
recall_cue: The customer says they have already written once. What do they feel, and what must your reply start with?
linking: If read aloud: this_is → "thi-siz" · second_email → "sec-un-dee-mail"
intonation: If read aloud: firm, with strong stress on "second".
indian_pron_tip: If you read it aloud, "this" uses a soft "th" (tongue between the teeth), not "dis"; "second" ends in a clear "nd".
customer_emotion: Frustrated and feeling ignored.
memory_hook: "Second email" is a yellow card: a third email may be a red card, so apologise and act now.
hindi_meaning: इस बारे में यह मेरा दूसरा ईमेल है।
hindi_roman: Is baare mein yeh mera doosra email hai.
simple_meaning: I already wrote to you about this problem, and nobody answered.
why_it_works: The customer feels ignored. They need an apology for the missed reply, proof you have read the first email, and an action with a time.
key_chunk: This is my ___ email about ___.
grammar_pattern: This is + my + ordinal number + noun + about + this
grammar_note: "Second" here shows the customer has written before; "about this" points to the problem.
tone_note: Apologise for the silence first. A reply that ignores the first email or starts "Thank you for contacting us" will feel like nobody is listening.
watch_out: ✗ Thank you for contacting us. Please describe your issue. → ✓ I'm sorry we didn't reply to your first email. I've read it, and I'm sending a new charger today.
dont_say: "We receive many emails, so replies take time." — it blames the workload and tells the customer they are not important.
positive_swap: Instead of "Due to high volume we could not reply", write "I'm sorry we didn't reply to your first email."
alt_1: I already emailed you about this.
alt_2: I'm writing again because nobody replied.
more_formal: I am writing for the second time regarding this matter, as I have not received a response.
ask_next: I'm sorry we didn't reply to your first email. I've read it, and I'm sending you a new charger today.
replies_you_may_hear: Finally. · Why did nobody answer? · OK, when will it arrive?
if_customer_pushes: Customer: "Why did nobody answer me?" → Agent: "You're right to ask. I can see your first email was not answered, and that was our mistake. I'm handling it myself now, and your charger is due to arrive on Wednesday."
cultural_note: Customers anywhere often write this when they feel ignored, and may escalate next. There is no phrase to translate here; the switch is for agents: skip the template opener and apologise for the silence in plain words.
channel_note: Voice: "I've called three times about this." Chat: "I already asked this." Email: find the first email in the thread before replying.
when_not_to_use: Do not answer with a template that asks the customer to explain the problem again.
mini_conversation: Customer: This is my second email about this. My charger is still not working. | Agent: I'm sorry we didn't reply to your first email. I'm sending you a new charger today. | Customer: When will it arrive? | Agent: It is due on Wednesday, and I'll email you the tracking link tonight.
source_rule: Apologise specifically, take responsibility, then give an action with a time.
fill_blank: This is my ____ email about this, because nobody answered the first one.
mcq_question: A customer writes "This is my second email about this." What should your reply start with?
mcq_options: A) A thank-you for contacting us, then a request for the customer's details. | B) A request to describe the problem again, so that you can open a new ticket. | C) A link to the help centre, so that the customer can find the answer alone. | D) An apology for missing their first email, then an action with a time.
mcq_why: The customer feels ignored, so apologise for the silence and act. A sounds polite, but it treats the email as new, B makes the customer start again, and C sends them away.
reorder_task: second / is / This / email / my
reorder_answer: This is my second email.
hindi_to_english: Customer se maafi maangiye ki unke pehle email ka jawaab nahin diya gaya, aur bataiye ki aap aaj replacement bhej rahe hain.
hindi_to_english_answer: I'm sorry we didn't reply to your first email. I'm sending your replacement today.
whats_next_customer: Who can I contact if the charger does not arrive?
whats_next_reply: Reply to this email and it will come straight to me. I will check the tracking on Wednesday and write to you if there is a delay.
role_play: Partner A writes a second email about a broken charger after getting no reply. Partner B replies with an apology for the silence, proof they read the first email and an action with a date.
record_task: Write a reply to "This is my second email about this." about a missing refund: apologise for the silence, show you read the first email and give a date. Send it as text or a photo for audit.
self_check: Did you apologise for the missed reply? · Did you show you read the first email? · Did you give an action with a time?

sentence: Hi David, thank you for your email. I understand that your order 52817 arrived without the charger, and you'd like one sent to you as soon as possible.
speaker: Agent
situation: A customer has emailed to say his new laptop came without its charger, and you are writing the first lines of your reply.
recall_cue: A customer's email is long and a bit angry. Before you offer any fix, what should the first lines of your reply show him?
stress: hi DA-vid · THANK you for your E-mail · i un-der-STAND that your OR-der · ar-RIVED with-OUT the CHAR-ger · you'd LIKE one SENT to you · as SOON as POS-si-ble
linking: If read aloud: thank_you → "thang-kyoo" · arrived_without → "a-rive-dwith-out" · sent_to_you → "sen-tuh-yoo"
intonation: If read aloud: a small pause after "email", a level or slightly rising tone on "charger" because the sentence is not finished, then a clear fall on "possible" to show you have the full picture.
indian_pron_tip: If read aloud: "without" starts with rounded lips for "w" (not teeth on lip, "vithout"), and its "th" is soft with the tongue between the teeth, not a hard "d".
customer_emotion: Annoyed that a new product is incomplete and worried he will have to explain it all again.
memory_hook: Think of a doctor who repeats your symptoms back before writing the prescription: you trust the medicine because you know she listened.
hindi_meaning: नमस्ते डेविड, आपके ईमेल के लिए धन्यवाद। मैं समझता/समझती हूँ कि आपका ऑर्डर 52817 बिना चार्जर के पहुँचा, और आप चाहते हैं कि आपको एक चार्जर जल्द से जल्द भेज दिया जाए।
hindi_roman: Namaste David, aapke email ke liye dhanyavaad. Main samajhta/samajhti hoon ki aapka order 52817 bina charger ke pahuncha, aur aap chahte hain ki aapko ek charger jald se jald bhej diya jaaye.
simple_meaning: Thanks for writing, David. Your order came without the charger, and you want us to send it quickly. I understand the problem.
why_it_works: Restating the problem in one sentence proves you read the whole email and lets the customer correct you before you act. It also prevents a second email that starts "As I already said…".
key_chunk: I understand that ___, and you'd like ___.
grammar_pattern: I understand that + past simple (what happened) + and you'd like + object + past participle
grammar_note: "Arrived" is past simple for what happened; "you'd like" is a polite way to say what the customer wants.
tone_note: Naming his exact problem sounds attentive. Starting with "We have received your query regarding the above" sounds like a machine and tells him nothing.
watch_out: ✗ I understood your problem that charger is not came. → ✓ I understand that your order arrived without the charger.
dont_say: "Your query has been noted." It is cold, says nothing about his problem and gives no sign that anyone read the email.
positive_swap: Instead of "We have received your complaint regarding the above order", say "I understand that your order 52817 arrived without the charger."
alt_1: Hi David, thanks for getting in touch. I'm sorry to hear that the charger was missing from order 52817, and I can see you need it quickly.
alt_2: Hi David, thank you for writing to us. If I've understood correctly, your laptop arrived but the charger was not in the box.
more_formal: Dear Mr Hughes, thank you for your email. I understand that order 52817 was delivered without its charger and that you would like the missing item sent urgently.
ask_next: I've checked your order and arranged for a charger to be sent to you today by express delivery, and you will receive a tracking link by email this evening.
replies_you_may_hear: Yes, that's right. · Not exactly, the cable is there but the adapter is missing. · Correct, and I need it before Friday.
if_customer_pushes: Customer: "I don't need you to repeat my email, just send the charger." → Agent: "Of course. The charger is being sent today, and I'll email you the tracking link this evening."
cultural_note: Indian business emails often open with "This is with reference to your mail dated…". International customers may not expect this; one plain sentence about their actual problem feels more personal.
channel_note: Voice: "So, if I've understood correctly, the charger was missing. Is that right?" Chat: "I can see your charger was missing from order 52817."
when_not_to_use: Do not restate a long, sensitive complaint word for word; summarise it in one neutral sentence instead.
mini_conversation: Customer: My laptop came without a charger. Order 52817. | Agent: Hi David, thank you for your email. I understand that your order 52817 arrived without the charger, and you'd like one sent to you as soon as possible. | Customer: Yes, exactly. | Agent: I've arranged for a charger to go out today by express delivery.
source_rule: Paraphrase before solving: restate the problem so the customer can confirm it.
fill_blank: I understand that your order 52817 arrived ____ the charger.
mcq_question: Which opening line shows the customer most clearly that you read his email?
mcq_options: A) We have received your email regarding the above matter. | B) Thank you for contacting us. Your query is important to us. | C) I understand that your order 52817 arrived without the charger. | D) Your email has been forwarded to the relevant team for review.
mcq_why: C names his order and his exact problem. B is tempting because it is polite, but it could be sent to anyone about anything. A and D only report what happened to the email.
reorder_task: the / arrived / understand / I / your / charger / order / without
reorder_answer: I understand your order arrived without the charger
hindi_to_english: Main samajhti hoon ki aapka parcel galat address par pahuncha, aur aap chahte hain ki use dobara bheja jaaye.
hindi_to_english_answer: I understand that your parcel was delivered to the wrong address, and you'd like it sent again.
whats_next_customer: Yes, that's right. When will the charger arrive?
whats_next_reply: It will go out today by express delivery, so you should have it by Thursday. I'll email you the tracking link this evening.
role_play: Partner A writes a three-line complaint email about a missing item. Partner B writes the first two lines of the reply, restating the exact problem and what A wants.
record_task: Write the opening two lines of a reply to a customer whose blender arrived without its lid, and send it as text or a photo for audit.
self_check: Did you use the customer's name? · Did you restate the exact problem in one sentence? · Did you say what the customer wants?

sentence: Your payment was declined because the billing address on the order did not match the address your bank has on file for your card.
speaker: Agent
situation: A customer has emailed asking why her online payment failed twice, and you have found the reason in the payment log.
recall_cue: The customer's payment failed and she does not know why. How do you explain the reason in one clear sentence without blaming her?
stress: your PAY-ment was de-CLINED · be-CAUSE the BILL-ing ad-DRESS · did NOT MATCH · the ad-DRESS your BANK has on FILE · for your CARD
linking: If read aloud: was_declined → "wuz-di-KLINED" · address_your → "a-DRESH-yer" · has_on → "ha-zon"
intonation: If read aloud: fall on "declined", a short pause before "because", then a steady fall on "card" so it sounds like a fact, not an accusation.
indian_pron_tip: If read aloud: say the final "d" in "declined" so it does not sound like the present tense "decline", and finish "match" with a short "ch" and no extra vowel.
customer_emotion: Confused and slightly embarrassed that her card was declined.
memory_hook: Imagine a key that fits the lock but turns the wrong way: everything looks right, but one small detail does not match.
hindi_meaning: आपका पेमेंट डिक्लाइन हो गया क्योंकि ऑर्डर पर दिया गया बिलिंग एड्रेस उस एड्रेस से मैच नहीं करता जो आपके बैंक के पास आपके कार्ड के लिए दर्ज है।
hindi_roman: Aapka payment decline ho gaya kyunki order par diya gaya billing address us address se match nahin karta jo aapke bank ke paas aapke card ke liye darj hai.
simple_meaning: The payment failed because the address you typed is different from the address your bank has for your card.
why_it_works: It gives one specific cause in plain words, so the customer knows exactly what to fix. "Due to technical reasons" leaves her guessing and likely to write again.
key_chunk: ___ was ___ because ___.
grammar_pattern: Subject + was + past participle (passive) + because + subject + did not + base verb
grammar_note: "Was declined" focuses on what happened to the payment, not on who made the mistake.
tone_note: The passive "was declined" and the neutral "did not match" describe the problem without saying "you entered the wrong address", which would sound like blame.
watch_out: ✗ Your payment got declined due to address mismatching issue. → ✓ Your payment was declined because the billing address did not match.
dont_say: "Due to some technical issue, your payment failed." It sounds like an excuse and gives her nothing to fix.
positive_swap: Instead of "You entered the wrong address", say "The billing address on the order did not match the address your bank has on file."
alt_1: The payment didn't go through because the billing address on the order was different from the address linked to your card.
alt_2: The reason your payment was declined is that the billing address did not match your bank's records.
more_formal: Our records show that the payment was declined because the billing address provided did not match the address registered with your card issuer.
ask_next: Could you check which address appears on your latest bank statement? Then please use that address as the billing address at checkout.
replies_you_may_hear: Oh, I moved last month. · Which address do I need to use? · But my bank said the card is fine.
if_customer_pushes: Customer: "My card works everywhere else, so it must be your site." → Agent: "Your card itself is fine. The check that failed compares the address you type with the bank's record, and not every site runs that check."
cultural_note: Some Indian support emails lean on stock phrases such as "due to technical reasons" or "address mismatching issue". International customers may find a short "because" clause with the real reason easier to follow.
channel_note: Voice: say it slowly and pause before "because". Chat: split it: "I've found the reason." then "The billing address didn't match your bank's record."
when_not_to_use: Do not give a cause before you have checked the log; if you are not sure yet, say what you are checking and when you will reply.
mini_conversation: Customer: Why does my payment keep failing? | Agent: Your payment was declined because the billing address on the order did not match the address your bank has on file for your card. | Customer: Oh, I moved recently. | Agent: That explains it. If you use the address on your bank statement at checkout, the payment should go through.
source_rule: Plain language (ICMI): give the real reason in everyday words, not jargon.
fill_blank: Your payment was declined because the billing address did not ____ the address your bank has on file.
mcq_question: Which sentence best explains a failed payment to a customer?
mcq_options: A) Your payment failed due to technical reasons. Please try again later. | B) You typed the wrong address, so your payment was declined. | C) Your payment was declined because the billing address did not match. | D) Your card was declined. Please contact your bank for more details.
mcq_why: C gives a specific cause without blame. B is tempting because it is specific, but it blames the customer. A and D give no real reason.
reorder_task: declined / because / was / payment / the / address / Your / match / did / not / billing
reorder_answer: Your payment was declined because the billing address did not match
hindi_to_english: Aapka order late hua kyunki courier company ne galat pin code daala tha.
hindi_to_english_answer: Your order was delayed because the courier entered the wrong postcode.
whats_next_customer: So what do I need to do now?
whats_next_reply: Please update the billing address at checkout to match your bank statement. Your basket is saved, so you won't need to add the items again.
role_play: Partner A emails asking why a discount code did not work. Partner B reads a note (the code expired on 31 March) and writes one sentence explaining the cause, then one next step.
record_task: Write a two-sentence email explaining why a customer's parcel was returned to the warehouse (the address was incomplete), and send it as text or a photo for audit.
self_check: Did you give one specific cause? · Did you avoid blaming the customer? · Did you use "because" with a full clause?

sentence: I've approved a refund of £45.00 for order 61204 today. It should reach the card you paid with within 5 to 7 working days.
speaker: Agent
situation: A customer returned a pair of shoes, and the warehouse has confirmed the return, so you can now approve the refund.
recall_cue: The return has been checked and the money is on its way. What facts must your email give so the customer stops worrying?
stress: i've ap-PROVED a RE-fund of FOR-ty-five POUNDS · for OR-der six-one-two-oh-FOUR · to-DAY · it should REACH the CARD you PAID with · with-IN FIVE to SEV-en WORK-ing DAYS
linking: If read aloud: approved_a → "a-proov-da" · refund_of → "ree-fun-dov" · paid_with → "pay-dwith"
intonation: If read aloud: fall on "today", pause, then slow down for the numbers "five to seven working days" so they are heard clearly.
indian_pron_tip: If read aloud: in the noun "REfund" stress the first syllable; keep the final "d" in "approved" and "paid", and say "working" with rounded lips for "w", not "vorking".
customer_emotion: Relieved but still unsure when the money will actually arrive.
memory_hook: A refund email is like a train ticket: it must show the amount, the departure (today) and the arrival time (5 to 7 working days).
hindi_meaning: मैंने आज ऑर्डर 61204 के लिए £45.00 का रिफ़ंड मंज़ूर कर दिया है। यह 5 से 7 कामकाजी दिनों में उसी कार्ड में पहुँच जाना चाहिए जिससे आपने पेमेंट किया था।
hindi_roman: Maine aaj order 61204 ke liye £45.00 ka refund manzoor kar diya hai. Yeh 5 se 7 kaamkaaji dinon mein usi card mein pahunch jaana chahiye jisse aapne payment kiya tha.
simple_meaning: We said yes to your refund today. The money should be back on your card in about a week.
why_it_works: The exact amount, the order number and a time range answer the customer's real questions at once. Without a timeline, the customer has to guess and may write again to ask where the money is.
key_chunk: I've approved a refund of ___ for ___. It should reach ___ within ___.
grammar_pattern: I've + past participle + today · It should + base verb + within + time period
grammar_note: "Should" means you expect it, but the bank controls the last step, so you do not promise an exact day.
tone_note: "Should reach … within 5 to 7 working days" is honest and specific. "It will be credited shortly" sounds vague and invites another email.
watch_out: ✗ Refund is initiated, you will get it in 5-7 days. → ✓ I've approved a refund of £45.00 for order 61204. It should reach your card within 5 to 7 working days.
dont_say: "Your refund has been processed and will be credited shortly." "Shortly" means different things to different people, so the customer cannot plan.
positive_swap: Instead of "Refund will be done soon, please wait", say "It should reach the card you paid with within 5 to 7 working days."
alt_1: Good news: your refund of £45.00 for order 61204 was approved today and should be back on your card within 5 to 7 working days.
alt_2: I've refunded £45.00 to the card you used for order 61204. Your bank may take 5 to 7 working days to show it.
more_formal: I can confirm that a refund of £45.00 for order 61204 was authorised today. Please allow 5 to 7 working days for the amount to appear on your statement.
ask_next: If it has not arrived by 24 May, just reply to this email and I'll check it with our payments team.
replies_you_may_hear: Thank you, that's great. · Why does it take a whole week? · Can you send it to a different card?
if_customer_pushes: Customer: "Why does it take a week when you took my money in seconds?" → Agent: "I understand. We sent the refund today; the 5 to 7 days is the time your bank needs to process it."
cultural_note: Indian support emails often use "initiated" and "credited". International customers may find "approved" and "should reach your card" clearer.
channel_note: Voice: say the amount and dates slowly and offer to repeat them. Chat: send the amount in one message and the timeline in the next.
when_not_to_use: Do not send this before the refund is actually approved in the system; promise only what has happened.
mini_conversation: Customer: Have you received my returned shoes? | Agent: Yes. I've approved a refund of £45.00 for order 61204 today. It should reach the card you paid with within 5 to 7 working days. | Customer: Great, thanks. | Agent: If it hasn't arrived by 24 May, just reply to this email and I'll check it.
source_rule: Use "I will" plus a time: give a specific timeline, not "soon" or "shortly".
fill_blank: It should ____ the card you paid with within 5 to 7 working days.
mcq_question: Which line gives the customer the clearest refund update?
mcq_options: A) Your refund is being processed. You will be notified once the amount is credited. | B) Your refund has been processed and will be credited to your account shortly. | C) I've approved £45.00 today. It should reach your card within 5 to 7 working days. | D) Please allow a few days for the amount to appear, then check your account.
mcq_why: C gives the amount, the date and a time range. B is tempting because it sounds positive, but "shortly" gives no real timeline. A and D give no time range either.
reorder_task: refund / approved / I've / today / your
reorder_answer: I've approved your refund today
hindi_to_english: Maine aapka ₹2,000 ka refund aaj approve kar diya hai. Yeh 5 se 7 working days mein aapke account mein aa jaana chahiye.
hindi_to_english_answer: I've approved your refund of ₹2,000 today. It should reach your account within 5 to 7 working days.
whats_next_customer: Will I get a confirmation when it's sent?
whats_next_reply: Yes. You'll receive an automatic email with the refund reference today, and you can reply to it if anything looks wrong.
role_play: Partner A asks by email when the refund for a returned kettle will arrive. Partner B replies with the amount, the order number, today's approval and a 5 to 7 working day timeline.
record_task: Write a two-sentence refund confirmation for order 33019 (₹1,250, approved today), and send it as text or a photo for audit.
self_check: Did you give the exact amount and order number? · Did you give a time range? · Did you avoid "shortly" and "soon"?

sentence: To look into this, I'll need a few more details. Could you please send me: 1. your order number, 2. a photo of the damaged item, and 3. the date it was delivered?
speaker: Agent
situation: A customer has emailed "my order came broken" with no order number, photo or date, so you cannot open a claim yet.
recall_cue: The customer's email is missing three things you need. How do you ask for all of them at once, so you don't need three more emails?
stress: to LOOK in-to THIS · i'll NEED a FEW more DE-tails · could you PLEASE SEND me · your OR-der NUM-ber · a PHO-to of the DAM-aged I-tem · the DATE it was de-LIV-ered
linking: If read aloud: look_into → "loo-kin-too" · need_a → "nee-da" · send_me → "sen-me"
intonation: If read aloud: a short pause before each number, a slight rise on each item, and a fall on "delivered" to close the list.
indian_pron_tip: If read aloud: "damaged" ends in a soft "jd" sound (DAM-ijd); do not say "da-maged" with a long "a", and keep the final "d" in "delivered".
customer_emotion: Upset about the broken item and impatient to get it replaced.
memory_hook: Think of a shopping list on the fridge: one list, three items, one trip to the shop instead of three.
hindi_meaning: इसकी जाँच करने के लिए मुझे कुछ और जानकारी चाहिए। क्या आप कृपया मुझे भेज सकते हैं: 1. आपका ऑर्डर नंबर, 2. खराब सामान की फ़ोटो, और 3. डिलीवरी की तारीख?
hindi_roman: Iski jaanch karne ke liye mujhe kuch aur jaankari chahiye. Kya aap kripya mujhe bhej sakte hain: 1. aapka order number, 2. kharab saamaan ki photo, aur 3. delivery ki taareekh?
simple_meaning: I need three things from you to check this: your order number, a picture of the broken item and the delivery date.
why_it_works: A numbered list lets the customer answer everything in one reply. Asking one question per email turns a simple claim into a long back-and-forth.
key_chunk: Could you please send me: 1. ___, 2. ___, and 3. ___?
grammar_pattern: To + base verb (purpose), I'll need + noun · Could you please + base verb + me + list?
grammar_note: "To look into this" gives the reason first, so the request does not feel like paperwork for its own sake.
tone_note: Giving the reason and numbering the items sounds helpful. "Share the details" is unclear because the customer does not know which details you mean.
watch_out: ✗ Please share the required details for further process. → ✓ Could you please send me: 1. your order number, 2. a photo of the damaged item, and 3. the date it was delivered?
dont_say: "Please provide complete details." It does not say which details, so the customer guesses and you still cannot help.
positive_swap: Instead of "Your complaint cannot be processed without details", say "To look into this, I'll need a few more details."
alt_1: So that I can open a claim, could you reply with: 1. your order number, 2. a photo of the damage, and 3. the delivery date?
alt_2: I'd be glad to help. To get started, please send me these three things: your order number, a clear photo of the item, and the date it arrived.
more_formal: In order to process your claim, could you please provide the following: 1. your order number, 2. a photograph of the damaged item, and 3. the date of delivery?
ask_next: Thank you for sending those. I've opened a claim for order 40917, and I'll email you the outcome by 5 pm tomorrow.
replies_you_may_hear: I don't have the order number, can you find it with my email? · Here is the photo, it came on Monday. · Why do you need a photo?
if_customer_pushes: Customer: "Why do you need a photo? Just send a new one." → Agent: "I understand. The photo shows our team exactly what was damaged, so I can deal with your claim faster and you won't need to explain it again."
cultural_note: Indian business emails often ask the reader to "share the details". International customers may not expect this; naming each item in a numbered list is clearer.
channel_note: Voice: ask for one item at a time and confirm each. Chat: send the list in one message, each item on a new line.
when_not_to_use: Do not ask for details you can already see in your system, such as the order number linked to their email address.
mini_conversation: Customer: My mixer came broken. | Agent: I'm sorry to hear that. To look into this, I'll need a few more details. Could you please send me: 1. your order number, 2. a photo of the damaged item, and 3. the date it was delivered? | Customer: Order 40917, photo attached, delivered Monday. | Agent: Thank you. I've opened a claim for order 40917 and will email you the outcome by 5 pm tomorrow.
source_rule: Email body: use plain words and number the items so the customer can answer in one reply.
fill_blank: To look into this, I'll ____ (starts with n) a few more details.
mcq_question: You need three pieces of information to open a claim. Which email line works best?
mcq_options: A) Please share the required details so that we can process your complaint further. | B) Please send me your order number so that I can look up your account for you. | C) Could you please send me: 1. your order number, 2. a photo, and 3. the delivery date? | D) We need some more information before we can proceed further in this matter.
mcq_why: C names all three items, so one reply covers everything. D is tempting because it sounds polite, but it does not say what is needed; B asks for only one item, and A does not say which details are needed.
reorder_task: details / I'll / few / need / a / more
reorder_answer: I'll need a few more details
hindi_to_english: Kya aap mujhe apna account number aur bill ki photo bhej sakte hain?
hindi_to_english_answer: Could you please send me your account number and a photo of the bill?
whats_next_customer: I can't find the order number anywhere.
whats_next_reply: That's fine. Could you tell me the email address you used to order? I can find it from there.
role_play: Partner A emails "my headphones don't work" with no other information. Partner B writes a reply that gives a reason and asks for exactly three numbered details.
record_task: Write an email asking a customer for three missing details about a wrong-size shoe order, as a numbered list, and send it as text or a photo for audit.
self_check: Did you say why you need the details? · Did you number each item? · Did you ask only for things you cannot already see?

sentence: I'm sorry that your booking confirmation showed the wrong dates. I've corrected them to 12 to 15 June and attached the new confirmation to this email.
speaker: Agent
situation: A hotel-booking customer emailed to say her confirmation showed March instead of June, and you have already fixed it.
recall_cue: The mistake is fixed before you reply. What two things should the customer read in your first two sentences?
stress: i'm SOR-ry that your BOOK-ing con-fir-MA-tion · showed the WRONG DATES · i've cor-REC-ted them · to the TWELFTH · to the fif-TEENTH of JUNE · and at-TACHED the NEW con-fir-MA-tion · to this E-mail
linking: If read aloud: wrong_dates → "rong-dates" (no "g" sound) · June_and → "joo-nand" · attached_the → "a-tacht-the"
intonation: If read aloud: a soft fall on "dates" for a sincere apology, a short pause, then a confident fall on "email".
indian_pron_tip: If read aloud: "attached" ends in a "t" sound (a-TACHT), not "a-tach-ed"; "wrong" starts with rounded lips and has no hard "g" at the end.
customer_emotion: Worried her holiday booking is wrong and annoyed at the error.
memory_hook: Sorry plus done: like a waiter who says "I'm sorry, wrong dish" while already placing the right plate on your table.
hindi_meaning: मुझे खेद है कि आपकी बुकिंग की पुष्टि में गलत तारीखें दिखीं। मैंने उन्हें सुधारकर 12 से 15 जून कर दिया है और नई पुष्टि इस ईमेल के साथ लगा दी है।
hindi_roman: Mujhe khed hai ki aapki booking ki pushti mein galat taareekhen dikhin. Maine unhen sudhaarkar 12 se 15 June kar diya hai aur nayi pushti is email ke saath laga di hai.
simple_meaning: Sorry, the dates on your booking were wrong. I have already changed them to 12 to 15 June, and the new confirmation is attached to this email.
why_it_works: The apology names the exact mistake, and the next sentence shows it is already fixed, so the customer has nothing left to chase. A general "sorry for the inconvenience" with no action sounds like a template.
key_chunk: I'm sorry that ___. I've ___ and ___.
grammar_pattern: I'm sorry that + past simple · I've + past participle + and + past participle
grammar_note: Present perfect "I've corrected" shows the fix is finished now, which is what the customer cares about.
tone_note: Naming the mistake and the fix sounds responsible. "We regret the inconvenience caused" sounds distant and does not say what went wrong.
watch_out: ✗ Sorry for inconvenience caused, dates are corrected. → ✓ I'm sorry that your booking confirmation showed the wrong dates. I've corrected them to 12 to 15 June.
dont_say: "We regret the inconvenience caused to you." It does not name the mistake, take responsibility or say what was done.
positive_swap: Instead of "Sorry for the inconvenience", say "I'm sorry that your booking confirmation showed the wrong dates. I've corrected them to 12 to 15 June."
alt_1: I'm sorry we sent you a confirmation with the wrong dates. Your stay is now booked for 12 to 15 June, and the corrected confirmation is attached.
alt_2: Thank you for spotting this, and I'm sorry for the mistake. I've changed your booking to 12 to 15 June; the updated confirmation is attached.
more_formal: Please accept my apologies for the incorrect dates on your booking confirmation. Your reservation has been amended to 12 to 15 June, and the revised confirmation is attached.
ask_next: Could you check the attached confirmation and reply if anything else needs changing?
replies_you_may_hear: Thanks, that looks right now. · Is the room type still the same? · How did this happen in the first place?
if_customer_pushes: Customer: "How did you get the dates wrong in the first place?" → Agent: "That was our mistake, and I'm sorry. I don't know yet how it happened, but I've checked every other detail on your booking and they are all correct."
cultural_note: "Sorry for the inconvenience caused" is a common fixed phrase in Indian support emails. International customers may read it as a template; naming the actual mistake sounds sincere.
channel_note: Voice: "I'm sorry about the wrong dates. I've fixed them while we were talking." Chat: send the apology, then the fix, as two short messages.
when_not_to_use: Do not say "I've corrected it" unless the change is saved in the system; if it is still in progress, say when it will be done.
mini_conversation: Customer: My confirmation says March, not June! | Agent: I'm sorry that your booking confirmation showed the wrong dates. I've corrected them to 12 to 15 June and attached the new confirmation to this email. | Customer: Thank you, that looks right. | Agent: You're welcome. We look forward to having you with us in June.
source_rule: Apologise specifically and take responsibility, then say what you have done to fix it.
fill_blank: I'm sorry that your booking confirmation showed the wrong dates. I've corrected them to 12 to 15 June and ____ (attach) the new confirmation to this email.
mcq_question: The customer's booking had the wrong dates, and you have fixed it. Which reply is best?
mcq_options: A) We are sorry for any inconvenience this may have caused you. | B) We regret the error. Please check your booking again later. | C) I'm sorry the dates were wrong. I've corrected them to 12 to 15 June. | D) This was a system error, not our fault. The dates should be right now.
mcq_why: C names the mistake, takes responsibility and shows it is already fixed. A is tempting because it is a common phrase, but it is vague and offers no action. D blames the system instead of apologising, and B leaves the customer to check the booking.
reorder_task: dates / I've / the / corrected / booking / on / your
reorder_answer: I've corrected the dates on your booking
hindi_to_english: Mujhe khed hai ki aapko galat size ka joota mila. Maine sahi size aaj bhej diya hai.
hindi_to_english_answer: I'm sorry that you received shoes in the wrong size. I've sent you the right size today.
whats_next_customer: Is my room type still the same?
whats_next_reply: Yes, your sea-view double room hasn't changed. Only the dates were corrected.
role_play: Partner A emails that an invoice shows the wrong company name. Partner B writes a reply that apologises for that exact mistake and says the corrected invoice is attached.
record_task: Write a two-sentence apology email for sending a customer the wrong colour of phone case, saying what you have already done, and send it as text or a photo for audit.
self_check: Did you name the exact mistake? · Did you say what you have already done? · Did you avoid "sorry for the inconvenience"?

sentence: I'm writing to let you know that your order 70315 has been delayed by three days. It is now due to arrive on Thursday, 18 April, and I'll send you the tracking link as soon as it ships.
speaker: Agent
situation: Your warehouse has told you an order will ship late, and the customer does not know yet.
recall_cue: You know about a delay before the customer does. What must your email say about the new date and what you will do next?
stress: i'm WRI-ting to let you KNOW · your OR-der · has been de-LAYED by THREE DAYS · it's NOW due to ar-RIVE on THURS-day · the eigh-TEENTH of A-pril · i'll SEND you the TRACK-ing LINK · as SOON as it SHIPS
linking: If read aloud: let_you → "let-choo" · due_to → "dyoo-tuh" · as_soon_as_it → "az-soo-na-zit"
intonation: If read aloud: fall on "three days", pause, then slow down for "Thursday, 18 April" so the date is clear.
indian_pron_tip: If read aloud: "Thursday" starts with "th", the tongue lightly between the teeth, not "Tursday"; "three" is "th-ree", not "tree".
customer_emotion: Not yet aware; likely disappointed when reading it but glad to be told early.
memory_hook: Like a pilot announcing a delay before you ask: bad news, but you trust the airline more because they told you first.
hindi_meaning: मैं आपको बताने के लिए लिख रहा/रही हूँ कि आपका ऑर्डर 70315 तीन दिन देर से आएगा। अब यह गुरुवार, 18 अप्रैल को पहुँचेगा, और भेजे जाते ही मैं आपको ट्रैकिंग लिंक भेज दूँगा/दूँगी।
hindi_roman: Main aapko batane ke liye likh raha/rahi hoon ki aapka order 70315 teen din der se aayega. Ab yeh guruvaar, 18 April ko pahunchega, aur bheje jaate hi main aapko tracking link bhej doonga/doongi.
simple_meaning: Your order will come three days late. The new delivery day is Thursday, 18 April, and I will send you a link to follow it when it leaves.
why_it_works: Telling the customer before they have to ask keeps their trust. A new date and a promised next step turn bad news into a plan they can work with.
key_chunk: I'm writing to let you know that ___. It is now due to ___ on ___.
grammar_pattern: has been + past participle (present perfect passive) · be due to + base verb · as soon as + present simple
grammar_note: "As soon as it ships" uses the present simple even though it talks about the future.
tone_note: Clear and early sounds honest. Hiding the delay or writing "there may be a slight delay due to unavoidable circumstances" sounds like an excuse.
watch_out: ✗ Your order will be delayed by three days, it will deliver on Thursday. → ✓ Your order has been delayed by three days. It is now due to arrive on Thursday.
dont_say: "Due to unavoidable circumstances, delivery may be delayed." It gives no new date and sounds like you are hiding the reason.
positive_swap: Instead of "Your order is stuck and will not come on time", say "It is now due to arrive on Thursday, 18 April."
alt_1: I'm sorry to say that order 70315 is running three days late. The new delivery date is Thursday, 18 April, and I'll email the tracking link once it leaves our warehouse.
alt_2: A quick update on order 70315: it will arrive three days later than planned, on Thursday, 18 April. I'll send tracking details as soon as it is dispatched.
more_formal: Please note that order 70315 has been delayed by three days. The revised delivery date is Thursday, 18 April, and tracking details will follow once the order has been dispatched.
ask_next: If Thursday is too late for you, please reply and tell me the date you need it by. I'll check the options and email you today.
replies_you_may_hear: Thanks for letting me know. · I needed it for a birthday on Wednesday! · Why is it late?
if_customer_pushes: Customer: "I need it by Wednesday, this is useless." → Agent: "I understand, and I'm sorry it will be late for you. I'll check with the warehouse whether express delivery can get it to you by Wednesday, and I'll email you by 3 pm today."
cultural_note: Some delay notices say "We regret to inform you…" or "Kindly bear with us". International customers may find "I'm writing to let you know…" plus a new date and a next step more useful.
channel_note: Voice: "I'm calling to let you know your order is running three days late." Chat: "Quick update: your order will now arrive on Thursday, 18 April."
when_not_to_use: Do not give a new date unless the warehouse or courier has confirmed it; otherwise say when you will have a date.
mini_conversation: Agent: I'm writing to let you know that your order 70315 has been delayed by three days. It is now due to arrive on Thursday, 18 April. | Customer: Thanks for telling me. Why is it late? | Agent: Our supplier delivered the stock late, so it left our warehouse later than planned. | Customer: OK, Thursday is fine.
source_rule: Use "I will" plus a time: tell the customer about a delay early, with a new date and the next step.
fill_blank: I'm writing to ____ you know that your order 70315 has been delayed by three days.
mcq_question: Your customer's order will be three days late. Which line is the best way to start the email?
mcq_options: A) Due to unavoidable circumstances, there may be a slight delay to your order. | B) I'm writing to let you know that your order has been delayed by three days. | C) Sorry, your order is going to be late. We will let you know more soon. | D) We are not responsible for courier delays, so please contact the courier.
mcq_why: B is clear, polite and says how long the delay is. A is tempting because it sounds formal, but it gives no detail and sounds like an excuse. C and D give no new date either.
reorder_task: delayed / order / has / days / your / been / three / by
reorder_answer: Your order has been delayed by three days
hindi_to_english: Aapki booking do din aage badh gayi hai. Nayi date somvaar, 5 May hai.
hindi_to_english_answer: Your booking has been postponed by two days. The new date is Monday, 5 May.
whats_next_customer: Can I still cancel if Thursday doesn't work?
whats_next_reply: Yes, of course. Just reply to this email before it ships, and I'll cancel the order and refund you in full.
role_play: Partner B learns a sofa delivery will be one week late. B writes the delay email to Partner A with the new date and a next step; A replies with one question.
record_task: Write a three-sentence email telling a customer their course start date has moved from 2 to 9 June, with the next step, and send it as text or a photo for audit.
self_check: Did you say how long the delay is? · Did you give the new date? · Did you say what you will do next?

sentence: Returned items need to be unused and in their original box, because we sell them again as new.
speaker: Agent
situation: A customer asks why her return was refused after she had used a hair dryer for a week.
recall_cue: A customer does not understand why a return was refused. How do you explain the rule so it sounds fair, not like "rules are rules"?
stress: re-TURNED I-tems · NEED to be un-USED · and in their o-RIG-i-nal BOX · be-CAUSE we SELL them a-GAIN as NEW
linking: If read aloud: need_to → "nee-tuh" · in_their → "in-thair" · sell_them_again → "sel-tha-ma-gen"
intonation: If read aloud: a steady, calm fall on "box", a short pause, then a gentle fall on "new"; do not speed up on "because".
indian_pron_tip: If read aloud: "unused" is un-YOOZD, with a "z" sound and a final "d"; "their" starts with a soft "th" (tongue between the teeth), not "dair".
customer_emotion: Frustrated and feels the refusal is unfair.
memory_hook: A rule with a "because" is a fence with a sign on the gate: people accept it when they can see why it is there.
hindi_meaning: लौटाए गए सामान का इस्तेमाल न हुआ होना और उसका ओरिजिनल डिब्बे में होना ज़रूरी है, क्योंकि हम उसे फिर से नए सामान की तरह बेचते हैं।
hindi_roman: Lautaaye gaye saamaan ka istemaal na hua hona aur uska original dibbe mein hona zaroori hai, kyunki hum use phir se naye saamaan ki tarah bechte hain.
simple_meaning: You can return an item only if you have not used it and it is still in its box, because another customer will buy it as new.
why_it_works: It states the rule in everyday words and gives the real reason behind it, so the customer sees it is not personal. "As per our policy" hides the reason and sounds like a wall.
key_chunk: ___ need to be ___, because ___.
grammar_pattern: Subject + need to be + adjective + because + reason (present simple)
grammar_note: Present simple ("we sell them") describes a rule that is always true.
tone_note: "Because we sell them again as new" sounds fair and open. "As per policy, used items are not accepted" sounds cold and gives no reason.
watch_out: ✗ As per policy, used product will not be returned. → ✓ Returned items need to be unused and in their original box, because we sell them again as new.
dont_say: "It is our policy, we cannot do anything." It hides the reason and ends the conversation without an alternative.
positive_swap: Instead of "We don't accept used items, that's the rule", say "Returned items need to be unused and in their original box, because we sell them again as new."
alt_1: We can take back items that haven't been used and are still in their box, because they go back on sale as new.
alt_2: To be resold as new, a returned item needs to be unused and in its original packaging.
more_formal: Items may be returned if they are unused and in their original packaging, as they are resold as new.
ask_next: If the dryer has stopped working properly, though, it is covered by the one-year warranty. Could you tell me what is wrong with it?
replies_you_may_hear: But I only used it twice. · That's not written anywhere on your site. · OK, what can I do instead?
if_customer_pushes: Customer: "I only used it twice, it's basically new." → Agent: "I understand. Once an item is used, we can't sell it as new. If it isn't working properly, though, I can arrange a warranty repair for you."
cultural_note: "As per policy" is a familiar phrase in Indian business English. International customers may not expect it and can read it as a refusal to explain; a plain reason works better.
channel_note: Voice: say it slowly and follow straight away with what you can do. Chat: one line for the rule, one line for the option.
when_not_to_use: Do not use it when the item is faulty; then the warranty or a faulty-goods return applies, not the unused-item rule.
mini_conversation: Customer: Why was my return refused? | Agent: Returned items need to be unused and in their original box, because we sell them again as new. | Customer: But it stopped working after a week. | Agent: In that case the one-year warranty should cover it. I'll check your warranty and email you the repair options today.
source_rule: Don't hide behind "policy": give the reason in plain words, then an alternative (derived advice).
fill_blank: Returned items need to be unused and in their original box, because we ____ them again as new.
mcq_question: A customer asks why a used item cannot be returned. Which reply explains the rule best?
mcq_options: A) As per our policy, used items cannot be returned under any circumstances. | B) Returned items need to be unused, because we sell them again as new. | C) You should have read the terms and conditions before you bought it. | D) The system does not accept returns of used items, so I cannot help.
mcq_why: B gives the rule and the reason in plain words. A is tempting because agents often say it, but it hides the reason. C blames the customer and D blames the system.
reorder_task: unused / need / items / be / to / Returned
reorder_answer: Returned items need to be unused
hindi_to_english: Ticket cancel karne ke liye 24 ghante pehle batana zaroori hai, kyunki hum seat kisi aur ko de sakte hain.
hindi_to_english_answer: Tickets need to be cancelled 24 hours in advance, because we can then offer the seat to someone else.
whats_next_customer: So what can I do with it now?
whats_next_reply: If it is working properly, it's yours to keep and enjoy. If it isn't, I can arrange a free warranty repair for you.
role_play: Partner A asks by email why opened software cannot be refunded. Partner B explains the rule in one plain sentence with a reason, then offers one alternative.
record_task: Write a short email explaining why gift cards cannot be exchanged for cash, giving the reason in plain words, and send it as text or a photo for audit.
self_check: Did you avoid the word "policy"? · Did you give the real reason? · Did you offer what you can do next?

sentence: I'm sorry, the blue jacket is now sold out. What I can offer instead is either a full refund or the jacket in black, sent free of charge. Please let me know which you'd prefer.
speaker: Agent
situation: A customer wants to exchange a jacket for a blue one in a larger size, but blue is sold out in every size.
recall_cue: The customer asked for something you cannot give. How do you write the "no" so the email ends with choices, not a dead end?
stress: i'm SOR-ry · the BLUE JACK-et is now SOLD OUT · what i CAN of-fer in-STEAD · is EI-ther a FULL RE-fund · or the JACK-et in BLACK · sent FREE of CHARGE · please LET me KNOW · which you'd pre-FER
linking: If read aloud: sold_out → "sohl-dout" · can_offer → "ka-noffer" · let_me_know → "lemme-know"
intonation: If read aloud: a soft fall on "sold out", a pause, then a rise on "refund" and a fall on "black" to present two choices.
indian_pron_tip: If read aloud: the "th" in "either" is soft, with the tongue between the teeth, not a "d" (then, not den); say the "t" at the end of "out" in "sold out" clearly.
customer_emotion: Disappointed that the item they wanted is not available.
memory_hook: A closed door with two open windows beside it: say the door is shut, then point straight at the windows.
hindi_meaning: मुझे खेद है, नीली जैकेट अब बिक चुकी है। इसके बदले मैं आपको पूरा रिफ़ंड या काली जैकेट मुफ़्त में भेजने का विकल्प दे सकता/सकती हूँ। कृपया बताइए कि आप कौन सा पसंद करेंगे।
hindi_roman: Mujhe khed hai, neeli jacket ab bik chuki hai. Iske badle main aapko poora refund ya kaali jacket muft mein bhejne ka vikalp de sakta/sakti hoon. Kripya bataiye ki aap kaun sa pasand karenge.
simple_meaning: Sorry, we have no blue jackets left. You can have your money back or a black one, and we will pay for delivery. Tell me which you want.
why_it_works: It gives the reason (sold out) and then leads with what you can do, so the customer still feels in control. Ending with a choice moves the conversation forward instead of stopping at "no".
key_chunk: What I can offer instead is either ___ or ___.
grammar_pattern: What I can + verb + is + either + noun phrase + or + noun phrase
grammar_note: "What I can offer instead is…" puts the focus on the solution, not on the refusal.
tone_note: Two clear options sound helpful and respectful. "Exchange not possible as item is out of stock" is correct but cold and leaves the customer stuck.
watch_out: ✗ Blue colour is not available, so exchange is not possible. → ✓ I'm sorry, the blue jacket is now sold out. What I can offer instead is either a full refund or the jacket in black.
dont_say: "Sorry, we can't do the exchange." A bare refusal with no option makes the customer argue or leave.
positive_swap: Instead of "We cannot exchange it because blue is out of stock", say "What I can offer instead is either a full refund or the jacket in black, sent free of charge."
alt_1: Unfortunately, the blue jacket has sold out, so I can't exchange it. I can, however, refund you in full or send the black one at no cost. Which would suit you better?
alt_2: I'm sorry we can't offer the jacket in blue any more, as it has sold out. Would you like a full refund, or shall I send the black one free of charge?
more_formal: I regret that the blue jacket is no longer in stock. As an alternative, I would be happy to offer either a full refund or the jacket in black, with free delivery.
ask_next: As soon as you reply, I'll arrange it the same day and send you a confirmation.
replies_you_may_hear: I'll take the black one, thanks. · Just refund me then. · Will blue come back in stock?
if_customer_pushes: Customer: "Will it come back in stock? I'll wait." → Agent: "Our supplier hasn't given us a date, so I can't promise that. I can sign you up for a back-in-stock email, and you can still choose a refund at any time before then."
cultural_note: A bare "Exchange not possible" can read as brisk in business English, including Indian business emails. International customers expect the refusal to come with a reason and at least one alternative.
channel_note: Voice: give the two options slowly and wait for the choice. Chat: send the "sold out" line first, then the two options in a separate message.
when_not_to_use: Do not offer options you have not checked, such as a colour that is also low in stock.
mini_conversation: Customer: Can I swap my jacket for the blue one in size L? | Agent: I'm sorry, the blue jacket is now sold out. What I can offer instead is either a full refund or the jacket in black, sent free of charge. Please let me know which you'd prefer. | Customer: I'll take the black one. | Agent: Great choice. I'll send it today and email you the tracking link.
source_rule: Saying no by email: reason, then empathy, then an alternative, then a follow-up.
fill_blank: What I can offer instead is ____ a full refund or the jacket in black.
mcq_question: The colour a customer wants is sold out. Which reply is the best way to say no?
mcq_options: A) Exchange is not possible as the item is out of stock. Thank you for understanding. | B) Sorry, blue is out of stock. Please try again later or check our website. | C) We have many other nice colours on our website. Please choose another one. | D) I'm sorry, blue is sold out. I can offer a full refund or the jacket in black.
mcq_why: D gives the reason, an apology and two concrete choices. C is tempting because it suggests other options, but it leaves the customer to do all the work. A and B offer no alternative.
reorder_task: refund / can / a / instead / I / full / you / offer
reorder_answer: I can offer you a full refund instead
hindi_to_english: Maaf kijiye, yeh model ab available nahin hai. Main aapko poora refund ya naya model de sakti hoon.
hindi_to_english_answer: I'm sorry, this model is no longer available. I can offer you either a full refund or the newer model.
whats_next_customer: Can I get the black one in size L?
whats_next_reply: Yes, the black jacket is in stock in size L. I'll send it today, free of charge, and email you the tracking link.
role_play: Partner A asks to move a hotel booking to a fully booked weekend. Partner B writes a reply that says no with a reason and offers two other dates.
record_task: Write a reply to a customer who wants a late-night delivery slot that you do not offer; give the reason and two alternatives, and send it as text or a photo for audit.
self_check: Did you give a reason for the "no"? · Did you offer at least two alternatives? · Did you end by asking the customer to choose?

sentence: I've passed your case (ticket 48867) to our senior technical team, as they can check the server records. They will email you an update by 5 pm on Wednesday.
speaker: Agent
situation: A customer's account keeps logging him out, the basic fixes did not work, and you have escalated the case; the senior technical team has agreed to reply by 5 pm on Wednesday.
recall_cue: You have handed the problem to another team. What three things should your email tell the customer about that handover?
stress: i've PASSED your CASE · to our SEN-ior TECH-ni-cal TEAM · as they can CHECK the SER-ver REC-ords · they will E-mail you an UP-date · by FIVE p-M on WEDNES-day
linking: If read aloud: passed_your → "pas-chor" · email_you → "ee-may-lyoo" · update_by → "up-day-tby"
intonation: If read aloud: a short pause after "team", a fall on "records" to end the first sentence, then slow down and fall on "Wednesday" so the deadline stands out.
indian_pron_tip: If read aloud: "Wednesday" is WENZ-day (the first "d" is silent), and "records" as a noun is REC-ords, stress on the first part, not re-CORDS.
customer_emotion: Tired of the problem and worried that escalation means more waiting.
memory_hook: Passing a baton in a relay: say who has it now, why they are faster, and when they will reach the finish line.
hindi_meaning: मैंने आपका केस (टिकट 48867) हमारी सीनियर टेक्निकल टीम को भेज दिया है, क्योंकि वे सर्वर के रिकॉर्ड देख सकते हैं। वे बुधवार शाम 5 बजे तक आपको ईमेल से अपडेट देंगे।
hindi_roman: Maine aapka case (ticket 48867) hamari senior technical team ko bhej diya hai, kyunki ve server ke record dekh sakte hain. Ve budhvaar shaam 5 baje tak aapko email se update denge.
simple_meaning: I gave your problem to our expert team because they can look deeper into it. They will write to you by Wednesday at 5 pm.
why_it_works: It says who has the case, why they are the right people and when the customer will hear back. Without those, "escalated" sounds as if the case has disappeared.
key_chunk: I've passed your case to ___, as they can ___. They will ___ by ___.
grammar_pattern: I've + past participle + to + team, as + they + can + base verb · will + base verb + by + time
grammar_note: "As" here means "because"; "by 5 pm" means "no later than 5 pm".
tone_note: A named team, a reason and a deadline sound in control. "Your issue has been escalated to the concerned team" sounds vague and like the end of your help.
